A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OneForecast study and contain accessible main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Reordered appendices and renumbered forecast galleries can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original global and regional forecasting experiments, ensemble comparisons, cyclone case studies and component ablations, including Tables 1–3 and appendix forecast maps.

after.justification: v2 retains and revises original forecasting experiments and adds efficiency measurements, spectral analyses, quantitative extreme-event results and fine-tuning comparisons.

M1.justification: The graph architecture, multi-stream messaging, nesting mechanism and loss remain substantially unchanged. However, Algorithm 1 removes the final addition of the previous atmospheric state, while decoder Equations 32–35 revise inputs and residual/output expressions. These are limited changes to the written procedure; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: The ERA5/WeatherBench2 global and regional coverage, variables, years and two cyclone cases are retained. v2 introduces Best Track observations for cyclone verification, with Section 3.4 specifying their use for Molva; v1 Figure 1 labels both reference tracks ERA5. This is a limited verification-data addition, without a broader forecasting-domain expansion.

E2.justification: Fengwu is removed from Tables 1 and 2, although it remains in visual and efficiency comparisons. Figure 4 expands the comparison to IFS-HRES and released baseline versions, and new Figure 9 includes NeuralGCM and Keisler. Comparator membership and the distinction between retrained and released models therefore change substantially.

E3.justification: The stated training budget changes from 110 to 200 epochs. Table 2 changes initial-condition spacing from 100 time steps to 12 hours and replaces RMSE/ACC at days 4 and 10 with RMSE at days 7–10. v2 also introduces evaluations using 700 initial conditions, one- and two-epoch fine-tuning comparisons, CSI/SEDI and track-error metrics, and a revised ACC formula. These are reported protocol changes, not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds parameter/MAC profiling, Q700 and surface-wind spectral comparisons, and quantitative extreme-event and cyclone-track analyses in Appendix G and Tables 5–7. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's component ablations, normalized spectral-error plot and qualitative cyclone cases. The existing ablation variants remain the same despite terminology corrections.

E5.justification: Figure 4 changes from curves with shaded envelopes in v1 to curves alone in v2. Neither PDF defines the envelopes' statistical meaning or supplies repeated-training-run or seed counts, so their removal does not establish fewer runs. The 50-member forecasting ensembles remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and several forecast plots contain revised results. For example, OneForecast's four-day RMSE/ACC in Table 1 changes from 0.2954/0.9577 to 0.2732/0.8825 under revised settings; Table 3 changes its first five rows while retaining the two MSM comparison rows. New results include a 157 km track-position error in Table 7, extreme-event scores, efficiency measurements, spectra and fine-tuning curves.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1 and the complete Appendix A theorem and proof are unchanged. Equation 37 substantively revises the mathematical definition of ACC by moving the square root from the entire fraction to its denominator. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and unchanged conclusion retain the same central claims: unified global/regional forecasting, adaptive messaging to capture high-frequency information, and neural nesting to preserve global information. Abstract wording changes and additional evidence do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 qualifies the blanket ensemble-benefit statement to improvement in most cases, especially at longer horizons. New Appendix G discussion argues that accuracy matters more than computational cost and interprets limited fine-tuning results as suggesting further improvement potential. These add substantive qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 explains MLP versus ESMLP construction more explicitly, newly discloses 100 initial conditions for the existing ablations, specifies the MAC-count input shape, and provides Best Track provenance and access information. It also documents fine-tuning budgets and revises training instructions. Existing graph sizes, embedding dimensions, hardware and OneForecast code access remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pfaff et al. for the mesh-network/ESMLP component and Ying et al. and Lu et al. for the cyclone database. The related-work discussion moves from Appendix F to B with unchanged content, and the central positioning relative to previous forecasting methods is retained.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and local wording, standardizes WeatherBench2 and NNG terminology, adds an Impact Statement, moves related work earlier in the appendices, and subdivides Appendix G. Most of the main narrative and the conclusion remain unchanged, so this is a limited editorial and structural revision.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–7 and Figures 8–9, redraws the cyclone and forecast-comparison plots, and restructures Table 2 around four RMSE forecast horizons. Figure 4 changes panel order, legends and shaded-band presentation. The existing appendix forecast gallery is renumbered and reproduced at lower raster resolution, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The corrected stated ACC formula, clearer comparison regimes and added quantitative extreme-event, spectral and efficiency evidence make v2 more assessable than v1. The net gain is limited by incomplete event-threshold and fine-tuning documentation, removal of Figure 4's undefined shaded bands, and an internal inconsistency: Figure 8 shows a FuXi Q700 curve although Appendix G.2 says those data were unavailable. The additions improve support and transparency without resolving the evaluation's important reporting weaknesses.
